subject.title: [MiniMax] M3 native video input support with timestamp-scaling metadata hint (reference branch only)

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a MiniMax M3 native-video path now, and if so should it stay in provider-owned media-understanding or also add a core LLM/tool-result VideoContent/readVideo contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing the implementation shape would define provider API behavior, raw-media security policy, prompt/session semantics, and core content contracts that automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Split provider-owned MiniMax video first
options.body: Add a narrow MiniMax media-understanding/video transport path with explicit size, egress, retention, and regression proof before considering broader core content changes.

options.title: Approve a core video content contract
options.body: Define VideoContent/readVideo and transport serialization as a first-class core agent/session API, with compatibility and security review before implementation.

options.title: Defer to generic video tracker
options.body: Keep MiniMax-specific findings as reference material while the broader direct video upload contract is decided in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/27482.

recommendation.title: Split provider-owned MiniMax video first
recommendation.body: Add a narrow MiniMax media-understanding/video transport path with explicit size, egress, retention, and regression proof before considering broader core content changes.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is MiniMax M3 provider ownership and prior adjacent MiniMax media work.
